### last time {.smaller}

*  CIDR notation
*  switching versus routing
   *  recall: in this class, switch = layer 2 (real world: sloppier about this)
   *  on local network "switches" use MAC addresses to forward
   *  destination/source MAC address just for local network
   *  between networks "routers" use IP addresses
   *  IP packet contains global source/destination
*  routing tables using just IP addresses
   *  need IP:MAC address mapping --- "neighbor table" (or "ARP table")
   *  discover IP:MAC mapping by broadcasting requests on local network
   *  "gratuitous" broadcasts of MACs
*  ARP hijacking
